scenes.heading: How Strapi CMS Works
scenes.text: The tech behind the open-source headless CMS.
scenes.narration: Strapi is an open-source headless CMS. In this video, we look at what is happening under the hood, from the database to the API.

scenes.heading: Headless means no frontend
scenes.text: Strapi stores your content and serves it as JSON over APIs. Your frontend or app decides how to display it.
scenes.narration: Traditional CMS tools mix content and page design together. Strapi is headless. It only stores content and serves it as JSON, so a website, a mobile app, or any other client can use the same content.

scenes.heading: The tech stack
bullets: React admin panel, built with Vite
scenes.narration: The backend runs on Node.js with TypeScript. It uses Koa for HTTP and routing, and a database layer built on Knex. The admin panel is a React app, built with Vite in version 5. Almost every feature is delivered as a plugin.

scenes.heading: Content-Type Builder
scenes.text: You design fields in the Content-Type Builder. Strapi saves a schema file and builds the API from it.
scenes.narration: Everything starts with a content type. In the Content-Type Builder you add fields such as text, media, relations, or components. Strapi writes a schema file for you, and that schema is the single source of truth for your API.

scenes.heading: Four files per content type
bullets: Route: maps a URL to a handler
scenes.narration: For each content type, Strapi creates a folder under src slash api. It contains the schema, a route, a controller, and a service. You can customize any of these files with plain JavaScript or TypeScript.

scenes.heading: The Document Service
scenes.text: The Document Service in v5 handles drafts, publishing, locales and relations in one layer above the database.
scenes.narration: Version 5 introduced the Document Service API, which replaces the older Entity Service. It is one consistent layer for creating, reading, updating, and deleting content, including draft and publish states and translations.

scenes.heading: Your database, your server
scenes.text: A Knex-based layer runs on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB or SQLite, so the same project works on each.
scenes.narration: Strapi runs on your own infrastructure. Its database layer is built on Knex and supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and SQLite, so you can start small and move to a bigger database later.

scenes.heading: What happens on one API call
bullets: Koa router checks auth and permissions
scenes.narration: Here is one request from start to finish. The client calls an endpoint. The Koa router checks authentication and permissions. The controller calls the service, which uses the Document Service to query the database. The result goes back to the client as JSON. By default, the public APIs return the published version of the content.

scenes.text: Both APIs are generated from the same content schemas. GraphQL comes through an optional plugin.
scenes.narration: Every content type gets REST endpoints automatically, with filtering, sorting, and pagination. Add the GraphQL plugin and you get a GraphQL API generated from the same schemas, with no routing code to write.

scenes.heading: Schema in, API out
scenes.text: Define your content once and let Strapi generate the backend.
scenes.narration: That is Strapi in short. You define the content model once, and Strapi generates the admin interface, the database tables, and the APIs. Try building your first content type to see it in action.
